chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Ibn Muskhan from Ibrahim ibn Abi Ishaq from Sa'id al-A'raj who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a woman who performed tawaf around the House for four paces (shawat) while she was performing Umrah, then she became menstruating. He said: 'She completes her tawaf, and there is no other obligation upon her, and her Umrah is complete, so she may perform sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, and that is because she added to half (of the total tawaf), and her Umrah obligation has passed, and she should restart Hajj later.'

And that which indicates that the meaning of the two reports is also what we mentioned is that they contained the command for her to perform sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. So if he had not meant what we mentioned regarding the addition to half of the tawaf, the sa'i would not have been permissible, because sa'i occurs after tawaf. And that is permissible only if she adds to half, because she is in the ruling of one who has finished the tawaf. And that which indicates what we mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.اَلنِّصْفُ: Half (referring to the required amount of tawaf)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who becomes menstruating after performing four paces of tawaf during Umrah?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) ruling that a woman who menstruates after completing four shawat of Umrah tawaf is considered to have fulfilled her obligation, as performing more than half is deemed sufficient. This allows her to proceed with sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, treating the incomplete tawaf as valid, while requiring her to restart the Hajj ritual later. This principle highlights the Shia juristic view that partial completion of a pillar can suffice for validity under specific conditions, emphasizing the flexibility in ritual law.
